questions.question: Which of the following devices provides wireless connectivity to the client with LAN network?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wireless network adapters**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• A** wireless adapter** is a **hardware device** that is generally attached to a computer or other workstation device to allow it to connect to a **wireless system**. Before the advent of consumer devices with built-in **Wi-Fi connectivity**, devices require the use of wireless adapters to connect to a network.
 
• Wireless adapters are also known as** Wi-Fi adapters**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

 
• Wireless adapters often come in **USB stick** form, which must be plugged into a USB port of a computer or device. USB has become a universal standard for all sorts of accessory devices that plug into a computer or workstation device. Wireless adapters may also come in the form of **PCI network cards **that plug into a **PCI slot** on the **computer motherboard**. They do not generally plug into the **Ethernet port**. Instead, an **Ethernet cable** can connect a computer directly to a router or other device.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ec23cb83ae6d6a1251d92fb37940ecba37832dae3f03c5e7ea22746ab5b88858.png] 

 
• New technology has made **wireless adapters** somewhat obsolete, as new generations of portable computers generally have **built-in wireless connectivity** that can be enabled or disabled as needed.

These keys act as **shortcuts**, performing certain functions, like saving files, printing data, or refreshing a page. For example, the **F1** key is often used as the default **help key** in many programs. The **F5** key is used to refresh. The **function of these keys can differ by the operating system and by a software program**.

questions.question: In multiple document interface (MDI)

options.text: All windows reside under a single parent window (except model window)
Windows are separated from each other

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All windows reside under a single parent window (except model window)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In a** Multiple Document Interface (MDI)**, all child windows are contained within a single parent window.
 
• This is a primary aspect of the MDI model. The child windows can be moved around, minimized, or resized within the parent window, but they cannot move outside of this boundary.

 

 
• Although option (2) indicates windows are separate from each other, it's not entirely accurate in the context of an MDI.
 
• While each child window is indeed a separate entity, they are not separate in the sense that they exist independently of each other outside the parent window.
 
• They are separate in the sense that they can carry disparate content and be manipulated independently but within the same parent window. Therefore, option (2) is not entirely correct by itself.

**So, the best answer to this question given the choices would be: All windows reside under a single parent window (except modal windows)**

questions.question: To select adjacent icons on the desktop, you have to press the ______ key and then click on the icons you want to select.

• This functionality is consistent across various operating systems like Windows and MacOS.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __

• **Tab key**__
 __

questions.question: Permanent Memory of a computer is known as-
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**ROM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The permanent memory of a computer is known as ROM(Read-only memory).**
 
• In computers and other electronic devices, **read-only memory (ROM)** is a form of non-volatile memory.
 
• After the memory unit is manufactured, data contained in ROM cannot be electronically changed. Read-only memory, also known as firmware, is useful for storing software that is rarely updated during the life of the device.
 
• **Plug-in cartridges containing ROM** can be used to distribute software applications (such as video games) for programmable computers.
 
• Read-only memory refers to memory that is hard-wired and cannot be modified electronically after manufactures, such as a** diode matrix or a mask ROM integrated circuit (IC).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The memory **is **permanently** installed on your computer. This is a read-only memory. The working memory of a computer, also known as random-access memory. The hardware allows data to be passed through a device. 
 
• **Random-access memory (RAM) **is a type of computer memory that allows data and machine code to be read and modified in any order. It is commonly used to store working data and machine code.
 
• A **CD-ROM** is a data-containing optical compact disc that has been pre-pressed. CD-ROMs are a form of read-only memory that computers can read but not write to or delete.
 
• The electronic circuitry that executes instructions in a computer programme is known as a** central processing unit (CPU),** also known as a central processor, main processor, or simply processor.

questions.question: In MS Word (ver. 2007 onwards) what allows you to link to other parts of the same document, connecting text in one topic to another topic or bookmark?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Cross-reference"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In MS Word (ver. 2007 onwards) the **cross-reference** allows the user to **link** to other parts of the same document, connecting text in one topic to another topic or bookmark.
 
• The steps to insert a cross-reference are given below:
 
 
• 
 **Step 1: **In the Word document, insert the text which starts the cross-reference.
 
 
• 
 **Step 2:** Then click on the **Insert tab**.
 
 
• 
 **Step 3:** Then click on the cross-reference option.
 
 
• 
 **Step 4: **Select the reference type.
 
 
• 
 **Step 5: **In the **For which box**, click **"Insert the cross-reference".**
 
 
• 
 **Step 6: **By clicking the checkbox of **"Insert as a hyperlink"**, the users can jump to the referenced item.
 
 
• 
 **Step 7: **Click the** Insert button**.
 
 
 

**Thus the correct answer is ***"Cross-reference"*.

questions.question: 64 bits = ____________ bytes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__8__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **64 bits** is equivalent to **8 bytes**.
 
• This is because there are **8 bits in a byte**, and therefore, **64 bits ÷ 8 bits/byte = 8 bytes**.
 
• Bits and bytes are fundamental units of digital information in computing and telecommunications.
 
• Bits (short for binary digits) are the most basic unit of data, representing a state with one of two values:** 0 or 1**.
 
• Bytes are a collection of **8 bits** and are used to encode a single character of text in a computer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The term **bit** is a contraction of the words “binary digit”.
 
• A **byte** is a unit of digital information that most commonly consists of **eight bits**.
 
• In computer memory, data storage, and transmission, **bytes are the standard unit of measurement**.
 
• Understanding the relationship between bits and bytes is crucial for fields such as computer science, information technology, and data communication.
 
• Data sizes in computing are often expressed in terms of bytes, kilobytes (KB), megabytes (MB), gigabytes (GB), terabytes (TB), and so on, where each unit represents a power of 1024 bytes (e.g., **1 KB = 1024 bytes**).

questions.question: Which of the following ensures secure transmission of email data?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**SSL/TLS over SMTP**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **SSL/TLS over SMTP** ensures secure transmission of email data by encrypting the communication between email servers and clients.
 
• It protects sensitive information, such as login credentials and email content, from unauthorized access during transmission.
 
• SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is commonly used for sending emails, and integrating SSL/TLS adds an essential layer of security.
 
• SSL (Secure Socket Layer) and TLS (Transport Layer Security) are cryptographic protocols that provide encryption, authentication, and data integrity.
 
• This mechanism is widely used in email services to prevent interception of data and safeguard user privacy.

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Uses of SSL/TLS in Email Transmission:**
 
 
• **Authentication:** Ensures that the email server and client are legitimate by verifying digital certificates.
 
• **Encryption:** Protects data from being read or modified during transit.
 
• **Data Integrity:** Prevents unauthorized alterations to the email content during transmission.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of SSL/TLS:**
 
 
• Provides secure communication for email services, protecting against cyber threats like man-in-the-middle attacks.
 
• Enhances user confidence in the email system by ensuring privacy and security.
 
• Widely supported by modern email clients and servers, making it an essential standard for secure email communication.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• SSL is an older protocol, while TLS is its successor and provides stronger security.
 
• Most email servers today support TLS encryption, often configured to use STARTTLS for upgrading plaintext connections to encrypted ones.
 
• Proper configuration of SSL/TLS on email servers is crucial to prevent vulnerabilities and ensure effective security.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: A project manager is preparing an investor presentation that requires consistent branding, including company colors, fonts, and logos on each slide. Which feature of a presentation tool ensures all slides maintain the same design automatically?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Slide Master.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Slide Master is a feature in presentation tools like Microsoft PowerPoint that controls the overall design and layout of all slides in a presentation.**
 
• It ensures consistency across slides by defining elements such as background styles, fonts, logos, and placeholders.
 
• **Any changes made to the Slide Master apply automatically to all slides that use its layout, reducing manual effort.**
 
• It is particularly useful for presentations requiring uniform branding, such as investor presentations or corporate reports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Slide Layouts:** Slide layouts are predefined arrangements of placeholders on individual slides. While they help organize content, they do not enforce design consistency across all slides like the Slide Master.
 
• **Animation Pane:** The Animation Pane is used to control the order, duration, and effects of animations in a slide, but it does not affect the overall design or branding of the presentation.
 
• **Theme Variants:** Theme Variants provide variations of a selected theme, allowing customization of color schemes and styles for individual slides. However, they do not enforce uniformity across the entire presentation.

questions.question: What is a Trojan horse in computer security?

options.text: A type of malware that replicates itself
A program that seems legitimate but damages the system

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A program that seems legitimate but damages the system**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Trojan horse** is a type of **malware** that **disguises itself as legitimate software** to trick users into installing it. Once installed, it can cause harm by **stealing data**, **damaging the system**, or **creating a backdoor** for other malware.
 
• The name "Trojan horse" is derived from the ancient Greek story where a wooden horse was used to sneak Greek soldiers into the city of Troy, similarly, Trojan malware sneaks into computers disguised as harmless software.
 
• Unlike viruses or worms, a Trojan horse does not replicate itself but relies on trickery to spread to other systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Software used for data recovery** (Option 1) refers to programs designed to recover lost or deleted data from storage devices. These are beneficial tools but are not related to malware.
 
• **A type of malware that replicates itself** (Option 2) describes a virus. Viruses are distinct from Trojans because they have the ability to replicate and spread to other systems without user intervention.
 
• **Antivirus software** (Option 4) refers to programs designed to detect and remove malware, including Trojans, from a computer. This is the protective software against threats, not a threat itself.

questions.question: ______ of a computer system holds data and instructions to be processed and intermediate results of processing.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the **__Storage Unit.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Storage Unit** of a computer system holds data and instructions to be processed and intermediate results of processing. 
 
• Storage Unit is any hardware capable of holding information either temporarily or permanently.
 
• A storage device is an integral part of the computer hardware which stores information/data to process the result of any computational work.
 
• There are two types of storage devices used with computers:
 
 
• a primary storage device, such as RAM.
 
• a secondary storage device, such as a hard drive.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 **Unit**
 **Description**
 
 

 CU
 
 
**A control unit** or CU is circuitry that directs operations within a computer's processor.

 
It lets the computer's logic unit, memory, and both input and output devices know how to respond to instructions received from a program.

 
 
 

 ALU
 
 
**ALU** is a complex digital circuit with an AU (arithmetic unit) and a LU (logic unit).

 
Multiple Arithmetic Logic Units are in a computer, including multiple ALUs in the CPU (central processing unit), GPU (graphics processing unit), and FPU (floating-point unit).

 
 
 

 Input unit
 
 
An **input device** is any hardware device that sends data to a computer, allowing you to interact with and control it.

 
The most commonly used or primary input devices on a computer are the **keyboard and mouse.**
